If the goal is reaching Toronto parents who don’t already follow you, I’d look for a studio that can combine short-form creative + paid social + audience targeting, rather than a shop that only manages organic Instagram.

A few Toronto options that look relevant:

Arnold Street Agency — Social-first creative, content production, paid social and influencer partnerships. They specifically say they work with local Toronto and lifestyle brands. 
Arnold Street Agency

Potential fit: Reels/TikToks showing classes, coaches, kids' progress and parent testimonials, then amplifying the strongest creative with paid ads.

Neighbourhood Creative — Offers creative direction, photography/video, paid advertising, social media and experiential campaigns.
Potential fit: A more community-oriented campaign around “find your child's activity” or seasonal registration.

The Influence Agency — Particularly interesting if you want to use local creators/parent influencers alongside paid social; its services include influencer marketing, social, paid media and content.
Potential fit: Toronto parent creators producing authentic “we tried gymnastics” content.

Synonym Social — North York-based and focused on social-first content, management, influencer marketing, copywriting and digital growth.
Potential fit: If you want an ongoing content partner rather than a one-off campaign.

Good Kids — A larger creative/advertising operation offering production, paid media, social, experiential and influencer work. 
Good Kids

Potential fit: A bigger, more campaign-oriented push if you're promoting multiple locations or trying to build a recognizable gymnastics brand.

We Are Family Canada — This one is especially relevant strategically: they specialize specifically in kids, teens and families, including parent campaigns, social content, influencer marketing, research and creative. They're not Toronto-based, but they operate in Canada. 
We Are Family

Potential fit: If understanding the parent decision-maker is more important than simply producing attractive social content.

What I'd ask them to pitch

Rather than asking, “Can you manage our Instagram?”, I'd give each studio this brief:

Objective: Generate trial-class registrations from Toronto parents who don't currently follow us.
Audience: Parents of children roughly 3–12, segmented by neighbourhood and age.
Creative: 10–15 pieces of vertical video showing the experience, benefits, coaches, fun and parent/child reactions.
Distribution: Instagram/Facebook/TikTok paid acquisition, with retargeting of video viewers and website visitors.
Conversion: Dedicated trial-class landing page → booking.
Measurement: Cost per qualified trial booking, not followers or impressions.

That will make it much easier to distinguish a creative studio that can actually help acquire families from one that's primarily selling pretty content.

If you tell me your approximate monthly marketing budget (e.g. $2–5k, $5–10k, $10k+) and whether you have one Toronto location or multiple, I can narrow this to a practical shortlist and compare their apparent fit.
